references.text: Jesus' answer that the hour has come for the Son's glory to be revealed is repeated and expanded shortly afterward when he says that the Son of Man has been glorified and that God is glorified in him.
In his solemn prayer, Jesus asks that the Father glorify him so that he may glorify the Father, which directly connects to the statement that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
This verse describes how no one laid hands on Jesus until his hour came, emphasizing that the specific time for his glorification and death is a divinely appointed moment.
Here it is confirmed that no one took Jesus before his hour came, pointing forward to the time he himself proclaims has arrived in 12:23 so that he may be glorified.

Shortly before the revelation in 12:23, Jesus expresses the distress of his soul and asks the Father to glorify his name, which immediately leads to the Father answering from heaven and confirming that he has glorified it and will glorify it again.
The prophecy that the Redeemer shall succeed, be highly exalted and glorified, and that many shall be amazed at him is a direct precursor to Jesus' statement that the Son of Man must be glorified.

Here it is foretold that the suffering servant will see his offspring, live long, and that God's will shall prosper in his hand, and that he will be highly exalted and glorified, which is the core of Jesus' message in 12:23.
